text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Slovenian newspapers:

- Slovenia's Parliament will vote on the country's new prime minister on Wednesday. President Milan Kucan nominated acting premier Janez Drnovsek of the Liberal Democrats as his candidate for the post.
- The leftist United List of Social Democrats, the Slovenian Nationalist Party and the Pensioners Party (Desus) said they would support Janez Drnovsek.
- Slovenia on Tuesday took over the one-year rotating presidency of the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) from the Slovak Republic.
- Electricity companies repaired several damaged power lines to restore electricity supplies across the country after the grid was damaged by heavy snow and ice over the weekend.
- Slovenia's forest authorities said on Tuesday that some 160,000 hectares (395,360 acres) of forest had been damaged by snow and ice over the past weeks.
- The Government Office for Macroeconomic Analysis projects economic growth at four percent this year and says total employment should rise by half a percent.
- According to first estimates, damage inflicted on Slovenia's telecommunications network by snow and ice totals some 215 million tolars ($1.5 million), Slovenian Telekom said.
- The Economist magazine ranked Nova Ljubljanska Banka as Slovenia's best bank. Currently there are 28 registered banks in Slovenia.
- Slovenia signed an agreement on Tuesday to import some 235 million kilowatt hours of electricity from Bosnia per year.
- Drug maker Lek's issue A was the most actively traded share on the Ljubljana bourse in December, accounting for 30 percent of the month's overall volume.
